_note: Frozen change-reason codebook. Sub-types ordered specific->general; each row assigned to the FIRST matching sub-type (patterns are lowercase regex matched against deploy_reasoning). Last sub-type per cell is the general rubric reason and acts as catch-all. Built from mined high-frequency reasoning phrases + LLM-proposed names; validated by coverage + sampling.

internal_essence->junk.name: Index / meta / transition text
internal_essence->junk.definition: The line is an index entry, heading, cross-reference, or topic transition, not a substantive sentence.

internal_essence->junk.name: Comparative / taxonomic dispute
internal_essence->junk.definition: Compares species or reports a taxonomic/classification dispute without defining what the kind fundamentally is.

internal_essence->junk.name: Process / behaviour / development
internal_essence->junk.definition: Describes a process, behaviour, mechanism, or developmental stage rather than the animal's essence.

internal_essence->junk.name: Descriptive / observational only
internal_essence->junk.definition: Catalogs or describes morphological features without using them to define the kind.

internal_essence->junk.name: No definitional/ontological claim (general)
internal_essence->junk.definition: The passage makes no claim about what the animal kind fundamentally is; it fails the ontological-claim test the new rubric requires.

non_divine_teleology->junk.name: General principle, not a specific animal
non_divine_teleology->junk.definition: States a general law (natural selection, struggle for existence, variability) without characterizing a specific animal's function.

non_divine_teleology->junk.name: Uncertain / non-committal
non_divine_teleology->junk.definition: Reports uncertainty or declines to commit to a functional characterization.

non_divine_teleology->junk.name: Transition / meta text
non_divine_teleology->junk.definition: Index, heading, or topic-transition line that names animals but defines nothing.

non_divine_teleology->junk.name: Process / mechanism described
non_divine_teleology->junk.definition: Illustrates or explains a process or mechanism acting among animals without characterizing the animal's function.

non_divine_teleology->junk.name: Taxonomic / variability discussion
non_divine_teleology->junk.definition: Discusses species variability, inheritance, or taxonomic difficulty without saying what the animal is.

non_divine_teleology->junk.name: No functional characterization (general)
non_divine_teleology->junk.definition: Names animals but commits to no function/purpose for the animal or part; fails the new rubric's characterization step.

internal_essence->non_divine_teleology.name: Functional account, explicitly non-divine
internal_essence->non_divine_teleology.definition: Gives a functional/purposive account and the reasoning explicitly notes the absence of divine grounding, routing it to NDT not DT.

internal_essence->non_divine_teleology.name: Part/organ defined by function
internal_essence->non_divine_teleology.definition: Characterizes an animal part or organ by what it is for (organ of flight, etc.).

internal_essence->non_divine_teleology.name: Functional class / ecological role
internal_essence->non_divine_teleology.definition: Defines the animal by a functional or ecological role/class.

internal_essence->non_divine_teleology.name: Functional reading (general)
internal_essence->non_divine_teleology.definition: Reasoning treats the passage as characterizing the animal/part functionally rather than by intrinsic structure.

junk->internal_essence.name: Structural / taxonomic classification
junk->internal_essence.definition: Classifies the animal by structural or taxonomic position (distinct class, connecting link, group membership).

junk->internal_essence.name: Intrinsic-nature definition
junk->internal_essence.definition: Defines the kind by intrinsic organization or characteristic features (internal essence).

junk->internal_essence.name: Structure, not divine purpose
junk->internal_essence.definition: Reasoning distinguishes a structural basis from a (rejected) divine/functional purpose reading.

junk->internal_essence.name: Structural/definitional claim (general)
junk->internal_essence.definition: Reasoning treats the passage as a definitional claim grounded in internal structure.

divine_teleology->junk.name: Divine mention, not about animals
divine_teleology->junk.definition: Uses nature/design theologically or about humans/nature in general, not asserting a divine purpose for animals.

divine_teleology->junk.name: Design-evidence (epistemic) dispute
divine_teleology->junk.definition: Cites organs as evidence for/against a designer; an evidential dispute, not an ontological purpose claim.

divine_teleology->junk.name: Divine causation without purpose
divine_teleology->junk.definition: Mentions divine creation/causation but attributes no specific purpose to the animals.

divine_teleology->junk.name: Observational / processual
divine_teleology->junk.definition: Describes behaviour or a process; observational not definitional.

divine_teleology->junk.name: No positive divine-teleology assertion (general)
divine_teleology->junk.definition: No positive claim that animals exist for a divine purpose; fails the new rubric's assertion test.

junk->non_divine_teleology.name: Functionally-defined class term
junk->non_divine_teleology.definition: Animals named by a functional/ecological class term (domestic, parasitic, carnivorous).

junk->non_divine_teleology.name: Part/organ functional characterization
junk->non_divine_teleology.definition: Characterizes an animal part or organ by its function.

junk->non_divine_teleology.name: Functional account, explicitly non-divine
junk->non_divine_teleology.definition: Functional reading the reasoning explicitly marks as non-divine.

junk->non_divine_teleology.name: Functional characterization (general)
junk->non_divine_teleology.definition: Reasoning now reads the passage as a functional/purposive characterization of the animal or part.
